content: Within the broader regulatory framework, the DMRE places a significant emphasis on compliance monitoring and enforcement practices, particularly during the relevant period of 2020 to 2024, where a concentrated effort was made to elevate occupational health and safety standards across the industry. As of June 2026, the DMRE has continued to prioritize regulatory measures aimed at improving safety standards in the mining industry, reflecting a sustained commitment to mitigating operational hazards. A pivotal development in the DMRE's regulatory enforcement occurred in January 2023, when the department officially mandated the implementation of Level 9 vehicle intervention systems for collision avoidance in all mining operations [32] . This mandate integrated these critical safety measures into the Chapter 8 clauses of the Mine Health and Safety Act Regulations, representing a significant technological push toward enhancing mine safety. However, comprehensive publicly accessible information regarding additional specific safety directives issued immediately following the 2023 mandate remains limited, which may indicate either a delay in the implementation of subsequent new standards or a gap in the public dissemination of regulatory updates. The official DMRE service page, which is dedicated to mine health and safety resources, provides foundational information guided by the 1996 Mine Health and Safety Act but currently lacks detailed catalogs of specific directives issued after 2023 [40] . Consequently, industry stakeholders seeking actionable and current guidance must frequently consult recent government gazettes or targeted DMRE announcements to remain fully compliant with the latest regulatory expectations. To address broader structural frameworks for mine health and safety, the South African government published the Mine Health and Safety Amendment Bill in 2026, which seeks to comprehensively revise the foundational 1996 Mine Health and Safety Act [29] . While the provisions outlined in this legislative amendment hold substantial promise for future safety improvements and regulatory modernization, its formal enactment remains dependent on official proclamation by the President. As a result, the updated provisions may not have yet taken full legal effect or translated into immediately binding safety directives [29] .
